label: overlapping changed paths are batched, so two members that touch the same file share one gate
the prefix-tree proof is skipped, so a landing that differs from the gated union still continues
a filtered gate reports PASS, so the bisect's PARTIAL is carried as a full-gate verdict
old: if [ $fail -eq 0 ]; then echo "GATE_RESULT=PARTIAL"; exit 0; else echo "GATE_RESULT=PARTIAL:$why"; exit 1; fi
new: if [ $fail -eq 0 ]; then echo "GATE_RESULT=PASS"; exit 0; else echo "GATE_RESULT=FAIL:$why"; exit 1; fi

label: a marker is reused after its member's head moved, so a newer push lands on an old gate
the kill switch is ignored, so RSI_BATCH_VERIFY=0 still forms and reads batches
markers are written without the union gate passing, so members land on a gate nobody ran
PARTIAL is read as a verdict, so a filtered gate's diagnosis becomes a batch PASS
the dispatcher starts singles for slugs a batch already owns, so the members pay two paths at once
old: if [ -n "$BATCH_SLUGS" ] && printf ' %s ' "$BATCH_SLUGS" | grep -q " $SLUG "; then say "#$N $SLUG: in batch $BATCH_ID, skip"; continue; fi
new: : # batch members also started as singles

label: a landed tree that is not the gated prefix is accepted, so the rest lands on a broken chain
every member is sent back instead of only the bisected culprit
the outside-footprint retry's log line lands in the captured verdict, so a passing rerun reads as no verdict
old: say "batch $id: gate failed only on tests outside the union footprint (or known-flaky); rerunning once" >&2
new: say "batch $id: gate failed only on tests outside the union footprint (or known-flaky); rerunning once"

label: the survivor fallback re-enters --one for the culprit already sent back, spending a gate on the rejected head
the survivor fallback is not told which member was sent back, so it re-enters the culprit
